executive_summary:
In the window from 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25, ARI3 collected 4,087 raw source records from 80 outlet domains. Final signal evidence was deduplicated so exact mirrors and syndicated or translated versions of the same publication count as one report evidence unit. The editor retained 27 signals. The largest by item count are sneaker (61 items from 14 outlets), denim (30 from 14) and vintage (22 from 15). Half of the sneaker items come from two outlets, mostly release coverage. Denim leans on one Who What Wear denim package. Vintage is the most widely spread of the three, across 15 outlets, in celebrity looks, vintage shopping and archive-referencing collaborations.

Autumn footwear, outerwear and colour recur: suede (16 items from 11 outlets), loafer, trench, burgundy, kitten heel, ballet flat and leather jacket. Boho (9 items from 5 outlets) comes mostly from non-English Vogue editions, sheer from the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show and red-carpet coverage, and quiet luxury (5 items from 3 outlets) appears partly in headlines saying it is being replaced. The smallest clusters, with 2 or 3 items, are barrel leg, maximalism, wide-leg, workwear, Y2K and Mary Jane. These are patterns in the sources ARI3 collects, which were 89.4% editorial in this window. They do not measure consumer adoption or what people wear.

top_signals.name: sneaker
top_signals.evidence: Release coverage dominates: Nike Air Max, Air Force 1 and Air Jordan releases, the New Balance 990v7, Vans' holiday styles and weatherized versions of everyday sneakers. Collaborations include Union's slip-on Dunk, Kyle Wilson with Nike SB, MM6 Maison Margiela with Salomon, Molly-Mae with adidas, Jil Sander with PUMA, Burna Boy with On and Salehe Bembury's Spunge. Trend pieces cover brown sneakers, spring 2027 sneaker trends and the sneakers seen in London, including Italian-language Vogue Italia and GQ Italia and German-language Vogue Germany headlines (translated). A Nike croc leather loafer and a Timberland shoe roundup also matched the term.
top_signals.index_note: The signal has 61 items from 14 outlets, editorial 59 and retail 2, on every day of the window. highsnobiety.com contributes 20 items and wwd.com 10, so half the items come from two outlets, much of it release coverage. The editor labeled it recurring.
top_signals.human_editor_note: Editorial view: sneakers are forever.

limitations: Items are counted as style only when the ARI3 style classifier (frozen v0.0.2) gives a confident yes. On a 150-item prospective holdout of articles published after the classifier was frozen, its accuracy was 0.833, below its pre-registered 0.85 criterion (EXP-003A, H2 not supported). The editor reviews every evidence item used in this report.
In this window, 1,815 of 4,087 items (44.4%) received a not-sure prediction set and were excluded from style-positive counts.

In this window, 89.4% of collected items came from the editorial sector and 94.9% from the editorial group (editorial, trade intelligence and independent criticism). The stored corpus as a whole is 89.2% editorial sector.

The window has 0 items from social platforms, which are not collected, and 4 from resale sources. The report describes the language of the collected sources, not style culture, fashion consumers or the public at large.
Signal interpretation and evidence review are done by one editor.
ARI3 stores each item's headline and feed excerpt, not the full article.
0 of the window's 4087 items were stored before 2026-09-30, so their first-seen times are reconstructed from earlier records, not recorded as they happened.
Seven ambiguous lexicon terms (western, brat, demure, lace, bow, sustainable, glamour) are left out of every count until their uses are checked one by one.

Exact mirrors and syndicated, translated or lightly re-edited versions of the same publication across publisher domains are collapsed to one report evidence unit. The frozen source snapshot retains the raw records.
ai_assistance: ARI3’s deterministic pipeline surfaced candidate signals and bound the report to a frozen evidence snapshot. An AI assistant drafted the executive summary, evidence text, and index notes using only the locked report evidence, including translations of non-English headlines. The editor selected and merged signals, set labels and confidence overrides, pruned evidence, reviewed the drafted text, wrote the editor notes, and approved the final report.
